directions.question: Under what conditions is recovery of coordination a subtype of functional team adaptation, alongside adaptation that improves an unimpaired team or accommodates new demands?

logical_move.proposed_superordinate: Functional changes in team performance in response to changed demands
logical_move.relation: Conditional proper inclusion: P episodes that exhibit a cue-linked functional change can be members of G_P; G_P can also include functional changes without prior coordination impairment. P as supplied is not unconditionally a subtype.
invariants: functional outcome must be assessed separately from actions
applicability_conditions: A team-level change and a relevant cue are observed.
The change contributes to a workable team outcome; improvement of one individual alone is insufficient.
logical_move.not_a_synonym_or_extra_activity: Adds a testable change-and-function criterion and includes non-recovery cases; it is not merely renaming restoration or proposing an additional debrief.

directions.discovery_target: Distinguish restoration by resuming an unchanged routine from recovery through a functional adjustment.

queries: team adaptation Burke Stagl Salas Pierce Kendall 2006 functional change team response challenges PDF university
"Understanding team adaptation: A conceptual analysis and model" psycnet apa abstract

bridge_test.test: For a non-coercive decentralized team episode, identify impairment, cue, actual change, and restored joint capacity independently. Compare with unchanged-routine recovery and successful adaptation without prior impairment.
bridge_test.pass_condition: The recovery episode satisfies the adaptation criteria and the broader class has non-recovery members.
bridge_test.current_result: Only the existence and theoretical character of a team adaptation framework were securely retrieved from an institutional primary-article abstract; its exact subtype boundary and the decentralized-team mapping were not verified.

directions.novelty_reason: Separates functional change from return of function and directs inquiry to alternative adjustment trajectories.
unknowns: Whether any anchor episode exhibits adaptation rather than simple resumption.
Exact adaptation definition was not verified in an opened primary full text.
Decentralization and non-coercion are not established by this source.

fixed.subject: S: organizational teams with distributed decision authority; location distribution is not substituted for authority distribution.
fixed.condition: C: after disruption is temporal, with onset/end and causation unresolved.
fixed.scope: Non-coercive organizational coordination; no employee surveillance or military command.
fixed.outcome: P retains regaining workable alignment of interdependent activity after impairment, with restoration and a different workable arrangement both possible.

directions.changed: P is tentatively classified within functional response-related change; S and C remain fixed.
directions.finding: The Burke et al. primary-article abstract presents a multilevel, multiphase theoretical model of team adaptation and testable propositions. It does not establish that all coordination recovery is adaptation.

candidate_validity.reason: Conditional inclusion is logically explicit, but retrieved primary abstract does not verify the full proposed definition or transfer; unconditional P subset adaptation is rejected.

directions.question: Can recovery of a team coordination function be represented as an adverse-event coping trajectory within a broader organizational resilience process, while distinguishing it from resilience as a capacity?

logical_move.proposed_superordinate: Organizational processes for handling adversity over time
logical_move.relation: Proposed representation, not identity: a measured P trajectory could occupy a coordination-function-specific coping/recovery segment in a process containing anticipation, coping and adaptation. A process segment is not automatically a subtype of a meta-capability.
invariants: collective functional capacity under an adverse episode
observable trajectory rather than a personality trait
applicability_conditions: The disruption qualifies as an adverse organizational event.
The unit of the resilience model is explicitly restricted to the team or a justified team-to-organization mapping.
Coordination function and a recovery interval are measured.
logical_move.not_a_synonym_or_extra_activity: The broader representation includes anticipatory and adaptive trajectories outside recovery; simply calling P resilience would fail the type distinction.

directions.discovery_target: A process-level representation that makes before/during/after episode boundaries explicit.

queries: Duchek 2020 organizational resilience capability based conceptualization anticipation coping adaptation

bridge_test.test: Map the same decentralized team and its coordination trajectory to the coping segment, then identify anticipation or post-event adaptation that is outside P without changing the unit or treating a capability as an event.
bridge_test.pass_condition: A justified process representation preserves impairment and workable coordination criteria and has distinct non-P segments.
bridge_test.current_result: Search retrieval confirms the author proposes three resilience stages and a meta-capability. Direct full-text open failed at an anti-bot page. Team-level representation is untested.

directions.novelty_reason: Exposes the process/capacity and team/organization type boundaries rather than treating bounce-back terminology as explanation.
unknowns: Whether coping specifically includes the measured coordination recovery episode.
Whether an organization-level model validly maps to distributed team authority.
Temporal overlap and causal ordering of the stages.

directions.question: When can coordination recovery be represented as a special case of regulation toward an acceptable joint-function region, alongside regulation that maintains function without a prior loss?

logical_move.proposed_superordinate: Regulation of collective functional variables within acceptable limits
logical_move.relation: Conditional representation: encode workable coordination as an acceptable region K of collective variables, impairment as leaving K, and recovery as re-entry mediated by regulatory action. Broader regulation includes remaining within K through disturbances.
applicability_conditions: An explicit, collectively legitimate acceptable region can be operationalized.
Relevant regulatory action and its effect are identifiable.
Distributed decision authority is preserved in the model; no central commander or employee surveillance is assumed.
logical_move.not_a_synonym_or_extra_activity: Introduces variables, acceptable ranges and disturbance attenuation that permit a maintenance-versus-recovery comparison; feedback alone is an unverified additional mechanism, not the definition of P.

directions.discovery_target: State-space conditions and response variety required for non-coercive distributed regulation.

queries: Ashby introduction cybernetics regulation disturbance essential variables pdf

bridge_test.test: Specify collective handoff or dependency-function variables without individual surveillance; record an agreed threshold and evidence that distributed actions limit disturbance effects or restore the variables. Contrast spontaneous return after disturbance cessation.
bridge_test.pass_condition: The mapped P episode is explained by regulatory action while broader regulation has maintenance cases; the representation predicts which disturbances exceed available responses.
bridge_test.current_result: Ashby provides the abstract regulator/disturbance/essential-variable framing. No organizational episode or distributed-authority regulatory mechanism was retrieved.

directions.novelty_reason: Makes threshold, disturbance variety and response availability explicit and distinguishes restoration by regulation from unassisted recovery.
unknowns: Which collective variables preserve the meaning of workable coordination.
Whether distributed actors possess relevant responses and legitimate shared criteria.
Whether feedback is involved; it is not inferred merely from recovery.

directions.finding: Ashby frames regulation using disturbance, a regulator and essential variables, with permissible ranges and attenuation of disturbance effects. This is a formal framing; it does not establish universal cybernetic causation in decentralized organizational recovery.

directions.question: Is regaining coordination necessarily a subtype of collective learning, or only when experience produces a change in the team capability that accounts for recovery?

logical_move.proposed_superordinate: Experience-related change in collective knowledge or capability
logical_move.relation: The unrestricted inclusion P subset collective learning is rejected. A narrower learned-recovery subclass might fit a learning-change class, but a learning behavior that accompanies recovery is merely an additional activity and does not establish type inclusion.
invariants: team capability and a separate functional-outcome criterion
applicability_conditions: Experience-related knowledge or capability change is demonstrated, not just conversation or restored output.
A link from that change to recovery is separately investigated.
logical_move.not_a_synonym_or_extra_activity: Learning can occur without impairment or recovery, and recovery can occur without learning. Debriefing, asking for help or experimenting cannot by themselves rescue the proposed lift.

directions.discovery_target: A discriminating failure case for an attractive but overgeneralized predicate lift.

queries: Edmondson 1999 team learning behavior reflection action PDF hbs

bridge_test.test: Compare restoration via an already known routine with recovery involving verified knowledge/capability change. Measure learning behavior separately from the assessed recovery outcome.
bridge_test.pass_condition: Only the second kind could support conditional inclusion; the first is a logical counterexample to universal inclusion unless learning is independently demonstrated.
bridge_test.current_result: Edmondson distinguishes learning behaviors, including information processing and experimentation, from team outcomes. The study supports a learning framing but supplies no claim that P entails learning.

directions.novelty_reason: Tests whether a proposed superordinate class actually contains P instead of converting a possible antecedent into an abstraction.
unknowns: Whether any recovery episode contains enduring learning.
Whether learning causes recovery rather than follows it.

directions.finding: The retrieved primary field study concerns 51 manufacturing work teams and separates learning behaviors from outcomes. It offers no evidence for classifying all recovery as learning; the role definition requires rejecting that overreach.

directions.question: Can coordination recovery be faithfully represented as re-entering a feasible set of joint activity assignments within a broader constraint-satisfaction relation?

logical_move.proposed_superordinate: Satisfying joint compatibility relations among activity choices
logical_move.relation: Conditional proper representation: map team activities to variables, available choices to domains, and interdependencies plus a workable threshold to admissibility constraints. Recovery is the restricted trajectory from an impaired assignment to an admissible one; the broader relation also contains first-time feasible plans and feasibility without a disruption history.
invariants: joint admissibility rather than isolated member success
applicability_conditions: A finite variable/domain/constraint representation preserves the observed recovery criterion.
Relevant constraints reflect consensual organizational coordination and do not erase negotiation or conflicting criteria.
A feasible assignment exists; model feasibility is validated against actual workable capacity.
logical_move.not_a_synonym_or_extra_activity: An explicit encoding permits alternative feasible arrangements and constraint-conflict tests. Merely using the word fit or recommending a scheduling algorithm is insufficient.

directions.discovery_target: Which dependencies must be represented for recovery criteria to be preserved and whether incompatible constraints make recovery impossible within current options.

queries: site.ics.uci.edu Dechter constraint network variables domains constraints solutions

bridge_test.test: Construct an encoding from a scoped team episode, require operational recovery iff the encoded assignment meets the declared workable criterion, and check for false-positive feasible plans and false-negative workable plans. Preserve member authority in assigning choices.
bridge_test.pass_condition: The encoding preserves the recovery judgment, admits non-P feasible cases, and makes an independently testable constraint-conflict prediction.
bridge_test.current_result: The author institutional abstract verifies the CSP representation and solution criterion. It does not supply temporal recovery dynamics, a decentralized team encoding or an organizational validation.

directions.novelty_reason: Recasts interdependence as compatibility relations with explicit existence and alternative-solution questions.
unknowns: Whether workable coordination can be represented at suitable finite resolution.
How negotiated or changing criteria enter the model.
Whether feasibility of a plan yields capacity to execute it.
No algorithmic mechanism in human teams has been established.

source_checks.title: Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams
source_checks.source_type: Primary field study hosted by MIT
source_checks.retrieval: search-1 and successful open-1 PDF, printed pp. 350-351
source_checks.exact_supported_claim: Edmondson studies 51 manufacturing work teams and describes learning behaviors as team activities for obtaining and processing data, including seeking feedback, information sharing, help-seeking, discussing errors and experimenting; learning behaviors and team outcomes are distinct constructs.
source_checks.does_not_support: That every recovery is learning, that learning behavior guarantees recovery, or that the sampled teams meet the anchor decentralization condition.
